subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw move compaction and memoryFlush out of the foreground session lane, make that foreground maintenance preemptible, or accept the current shorter-timeout plus recovery mitigation?
rationale: The source-backed bug remains, but the durable fix changes ordering guarantees between interactive turns and session-maintenance work.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so new user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance to finish.

options.title: Preempt foreground maintenance
options.body: Keep the existing lane model but make compaction and memoryFlush abortable and reschedulable when user-visible work arrives.

options.title: Accept recovery mitigation
options.body: Treat the current 180-second compaction timeout and stuck-session recovery as sufficient, leaving active compaction windows foreground-blocking by design.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so new user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance to finish.

likelyOwner.reason: The open diagnostic-recovery PR and CODEOWNERS context make this the clearest current routing candidate for the scheduler/recovery decision.
